 Oral Jugment
1.

This appeal is filed by the claimant being aggrieved
by the judgment and award dated 8th August 2019, passed
by the Additional Senior Civil Judge & Jmfc & Member,
Mact, Puttur, D.K., (for short `Tribunal'), in Mvc
No.1623/2015, seeking enhancement of compensation.
2.  This matter is listed for hearing on Interlocutory application.
With the consent of the learned counsels for both the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

4. Brief facts of the case are that, on 18.05.2015 at about 3.30 p.m., the claimant while proceeding in a tipper lorry bearing Registration No.KA-19-A-6068 met with an accident and sustained grievous injuries.
He took treatment and has suffered disability.

With these reasons,
the claimant has prayed for awarding compensation.
Respondent Nos.1, 3 and 5 are owners of the respective vehicles.
Respondent Nos.2, 4 and 6 are the insurers.

Respondents-insurers appeared before the Sri Surendra B vs Sri Krishna Kumar S on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5221343/
3 Tribunal and filed their written statements.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 in its written statement denied the contentions of the claim petitioner and denied its liability to pay the compensation.
With these reasons, prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
6. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal framed necessary issues, for its determination.

MVC No.1623/2015 was clubbed with MVC No.1622/2015 and the Tribunal has recorded common evidences in respect of both the cases.
7.
The Tribunal after hearing both parties and appreciating the evidence on record, held that the accident occurred due to negligence of driver of the tipper lorry bearing Registration No.KA-19-A-6068.

The Tribunal assessed the injury sustained by the claimant; his income;

sentences.text: Heard the arguments of the learned counsel appearing for the claimant as well as the insurer.
9. Fact of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident are not in dispute.

10. On the re-consideration of the materials available on the record, the amount of compensation awarded towards special diet, conveyance charges and attendant charges  -6-  NC: 2025:KHC:44850  MFA No. 4940 of 2020 HC-KAR and loss of amenities are on the lower side.
The Tribunal has taken the income as Rs.8,000/-, though claimant has contended that he was earning Rs.19,000/- per month.
Following the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, income of the claimant is taken as Rs.9,000/- per month.

11. Considering all these facts, claimant is entitled to Sri Surendra B vs Sri Krishna Kumar S on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5221343/
5 enhancement of global compensation of Rs.30,000/- along with interest on the said amount at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim until its realization and respondent No.2 is liable to pay the same.

sentences.text:
12. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER a) The Appeal is allowed in part.

b) The judgment and award dated 8th August 2019, passed by the Additional Senior Civil Judge &
JMFC & Member, MACT, Puttur, D.K. in MVC No.1623/2015, stands modified.

NC: 2025:KHC:44850 HC-KAR c) The claimant is entitled for global compensation of Rs.30,000/-, with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
d) The respondent No.2 - Insurance Company shall deposit the amount within a period of six weeks from the date of award.
e) Since, amount enhanced is marginal, entire enhanced amount with interest shall be released in favour of the claimant, on due identification.
f) No order as to costs.
g) Draw award accordingly.
h) Registry is directed to send back the records along with a copy of this judgment to the concerned Tribunal.
